measured.contract: keeps the contract the mod's stock players share: their animations at their numbers, their shared bones, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Silhouette overlap is 0.82 to 0.84 in all six views, so the measure holds. Visually, the reproduction's boot soles are flat, squared blocks that stick out past the leg in the left and right views and in the front-left and front-right angles, where the original's boots taper to a toe. In the back views the reproduction's shoulders also read wider and squarer than the original's. Those parts are not on the original's outline.

M2.reason: Measured size, original vs reproduction: length 23.7 vs 25.3 (+6.8%), width 22.0 vs 22.2 (+0.9%), height 69.4 vs 69.2 (-0.3%). All three are within 10%.

M3.reason: Small parts of the original that are not clearly there in the reproduction: the boots' laces and eyelets (visible on the original's front and left views) read as plain dark leather on the reproduction, and the boots' soles are blocks rather than the original's lugged, tapered soles. The row of gold pouch items across the original's chest (front-right angle) is fainter and less defined in the reproduction. The balaclava, gloves, vest, belt, thigh pocket and knee pads are present in the right places.

M4.reason: Measured colour difference inside the shared outline: mean deltaE 3.1, every view between 2.3 and 3.7, shared area 0.79 to 0.84. Black vest and balaclava, grey-white camo trousers, black boots and skin on the forearms all read as the same colours and materials as the original.

M5.reason: The camo trousers are the clearest difference: the original's white-grey blotches are bright and high in contrast, while the reproduction's are greyer and softer, close to smeared, in the front, back and side views. The forearm tattoos are present but blurrier, and the 'SIT' lettering on the back is softer than the original's.

M6.reason: At game size and side by side, the reproduction is recognisably the same character, but a player comparing them would notice the blocky boot soles, the softer camo and the blurred tattoos. The line-up test for M6 is run separately.

M7.reason: The front faces the original's front, the model stands upright, and its feet sit on the ground line at the same height as the original's in the side views (the feet line up at about the same y in the left and right views). The top and below views show the same footprint and orientation.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty. Triangles are 1296 against the original's 873, which is 1.48 times and under the 2x limit. No open or inside-out parts and no floating parts are visible in the six views or the angles; the feet sit on the ground.

C1.reason: Across the run (30 frames), the attack (20 frames) and the forward dive (35 frames), every part stays on the body and moves with it in the frames shown. The arms, legs and torso keep their joints through the dive, and nothing appears to float or sink. The dive starts more crouched than the original's, which is a timing difference and not a fault.

C2.reason: The measurements report no contract fault: checkErrors is empty, and the contract line states the bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts were kept. The stunt's frame count (35 against 22) is a timing difference, not a contract item. The compareContract result itself is not printed in the input, so this score rests on the empty checkErrors and the contract line.
